`verify_bundle` delegates to `self._chain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)` which internally checks `proof["merkle_root"] != merkle_root`. Since `build_inclusion_proof` embeds the merkle_root at build time, a bundle whose proofs were built against a different tree state (pre-append) will have proofs with a merkle_root that doesn't match the bundle's `merkle_root`, causing all proofs to fail even if structurally valid. Independent evidence: the chain_hash pre-check in `verify_bundle` has a bypass. When `record.get("chain_hash", "")` returns empty string (malformed or stripped record), the truthiness check `if record_hash and proof_hash and record_hash != proof_hash` short-circuits to False, skipping the mismatch detection entirely. The proof's own `chain_hash` is then used for verification via `verify_inclusion_proof`, meaning a record with a stripped `chain_hash` field passes verification if the proof itself is valid — the record-proof binding is not enforced.
